## Glossary

**anticipated**  
Primary measure: share of real corrections some Warden said first.

**charter eval**  
scripts/evals/warden-charter.ts: runs a classify configuration over probes and judges the remarks; a dev diagnostic.

**classify run config**  
run.json given to --classify: stages, eval-only sections, debug, members; read by readClassifyRun.

**correction target**  
What a correction pushed toward (rule, primitive, system, pattern) labelled by --label-targets (Opus).

**cost weights**  
kindWeighted / modelWeighted: tokens weighted by kind and model into comparable cost.

**experiment gate**  
requireExperiment / experimentProblems: a wide eval run needs a passing experiment design.

**fails open**  
An unsure score, failed call, timeout or missing model asks the Warden, as without the pre-filter.

**fixture**  
A labelled moment (the Prospector's 740) used for pre-filter measures and label agreement.

**judge**  
Judges one Warden remark with the provider, retrying a failed call up to twice.

**Kev-4B**  
The local pre-filter model (Qwen3.5-4B + LoRA, MLX) served on the System One API.

**markEvalRun**  
Marks a process and state dir as an eval run so Archive and repeat reports skip it.

**Oracle**  
The replay test of Wardens; scores with the same foundry-core code as the charter eval.

**prefilter.enabled**  
Turns the pre-filter on; false (default) asks every Warden and starts no model server.

**prefilter.skipBelow**  
Score threshold (0.26): a Warden scoring below it is skipped.

**prefiltered**  
Journal field listing skipped Wardens with their scores on advice, guard and review records.

**probe**  
A moment from a real session: the user's ask, the agent's turn, the correction, and a train/test period; never committed.

**recall / skip rate**  
Share of relevant (moment, Warden) pairs still asked / share of all pairs not asked.

**silence precision**  
NO_COMMENT when nothing of the Warden's applied.

**speak precision**  
A remark matched the user's later real correction, judged by Opus.

**System One API**  
TypeSafe's decision endpoint (POST /v1/systemone), served locally on a loopback baseUrl for the pre-filter.

**TypeSafeDecisionClient**  
The client the pre-filter calls the local server through (lives in the `typesafe` region).

**warden-evals**  
Class: Warden eval machinery: probes, labels, charter runs, classify run configs, judging, cost weights, reports, the experiment gate.

**warden-prefilter**  
Class: the local-model pre-filter that may skip a Warden on a confident no; off by default, fails open.

**WardenPrefilter**  
Asks the local pre-filter model which Warden domains can be skipped for a trigger.

**wilsonInterval**  
95% Wilson interval for n successes in d trials.

## 1. What this Warden covers

Two measuring-and-gating jobs around the Warden chorus: the optional local-model pre-filter that may skip a Warden on a confident no (off by default, fails open), and the eval machinery that scores Wardens and the pre-filter against real sessions: probes, labels, judges, scores, cost weights and the experiment gate.

## 2. The domain

The pre-filter (WardenPrefilter in providers/warden-prefilter.ts, scoring helpers in core feedback/warden-prefilter.ts) sends one local call per trigger through TypeSafeDecisionClient to a loopback System One server (Kev-4B), asking per Warden 'Is this about …?' (prefilterQuestion over prefilterDescription and prefilterState). prefilterSkips skips only a confident no below `prefilter.skipBelow`; an unsure score, failed call or missing model asks the Warden. It is not a keyword or path filter; every skip is journalled with its score, and a missing or down server is reported in the daemon log, the viewer's event stream and doctor. It is off by default (`prefilter.enabled`) because no local model clears the recall bar; installPrefilterModel and startPrefilterServer only act when it is on. scorePrefilter (recall vs skip-rate sweep), prefilterConsistency (repeat stability) and `scripts/evals/warden-prefilter.ts measure` are how it is measured.

The eval side: runCharterEval runs probes built from real sessions (the user's own correction is ground truth), one turn per trigger with every Warden asked at once, composed exactly as a live thread composes them, then judges each remark (judge, wardenJudgeMessage / wardenPointerJudgeMessage, parseWardenJudgement / parseWardenPointerJudgement). Correction targets are labelled (correctionTargetMessages, parseCorrectionTargets) and canonicalized (targetCanonicalMessages, parseTargetCanonical); scoreCharterRun scores a run in foundry-core so Oracle scores the same way; readClassifyRun loads a classify run config; kindWeighted / modelWeighted give cost; wilsonInterval gives intervals; requireExperiment blocks a wide run without a passing design; markEvalRun keeps eval runs out of Archive and repeat reports. Source fetchers (fetchLinearItems, fetchReviewedPrs, sessionEvidence) gather reviewer comments as correction sources.

Not here: the charter text, stages and answer parsers the eval exercises are `classify`; when Wardens are asked at each trigger is `warden-triggers`; the chorus setting and region Wardens are `chorus`; the Prospector correction detector and `foundry repeats` are `feedback`; TypeSafeDecisionClient itself is `typesafe`; the decision host evals run on (decisionHost) is `decision-hosts`.

## 4. The specifics, in full

### 4a. Doc sections

Each unit is the doc section verbatim, with its headings shifted down two levels. A source line above it gives the path, the section and the doc's H1.

<!-- unit doc:docs/subscription-decisions.md#warden-pre-filter -->
**Source:** `docs/subscription-decisions.md` § Warden pre-filter (in "Subscription-only Foundry")

#### Warden pre-filter

**Off by default** (Aron, 2026-10-15: "leave pre-filtering on but switch it off for now until we figure out if we can make it work"). The code stays in Foundry; no local model clears the bar yet (below). Off, every Warden is asked on every trigger, no model server starts, `foundry-acp setup` downloads nothing, and neither `bun run doctor` nor the viewer mentions a model.

When turned on (`prefilter.enabled: true`), before a trigger point fans out to the Wardens, one local decision-model call asks, per Warden, whether the moment is about its domain. A Warden is skipped only on a confident no (its score below `skipBelow`); an unsure score, a failed call or a missing model asks it, as without the pre-filter. It runs at both ends of a turn: before (the user's message, the advice phase) and after (the turn's guard over its tool activity, and the post-work review of the finished turn), and at a handoff to a subagent (the brief).

- **Model.** Kev-4B (Jared Palmer, Apache-2.0: a LoRA and pointer head on Qwen3.5-4B-Base, MLX on Apple Silicon), served on this machine on TypeSafe's System One API (`POST /v1/systemone`), so the call is `TypeSafeDecisionClient` with a `baseUrl` (`providers/warden-prefilter.ts`). One request per trigger carries one yes/no question per Warden: "Is this about <the Warden's instructions, without its opener>?" over a bounded view of the moment and the thread state (core `feedback/warden-prefilter.ts`). The moment never leaves the machine: `baseUrl` must be loopback.
- **Install.** Opt-in: `foundry-acp setup` installs it only when the daemon's settings turn the pre-filter on (`providers/prefilter-model.ts`): the pinned server source, its uv environment and the pinned weights, all under `~/.foundry/models` (`FOUNDRY_MODELS` overrides), about 9 GB. It needs `uv` (`brew install uv`) and `git`. The daemon starts the server at its own start (so turning it on needs a daemon restart) on the `decisions` port, 8680 in Foundry's block (registry entry pending in inixiative/config#8; the code's default does not read the registry), and stops it on shutdown; a server already answering there is used as is.
- **On, but missing or down.** Every Warden is asked, exactly as without it. The daemon log, the viewer's event stream (`warden-prefilter`, a warning) and `bun run doctor` (`prefilter-not-installed` or `prefilter-unavailable`, warnings, never errors) say so. Nothing is silent.
- **Journal.** Every skip is recorded with its score: the advice row's `prefiltered` list and `prefilter` call (`status`, `elapsedMs`, `skipped`), the guard outcome's `prefiltered`, and a review's `prefiltered` learning record (`pre-filter score 0.031 < 0.1`). Oracle can audit the misses.
- **Settings.** `prefilter`, off by default:

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `prefilter.enabled` | `false` | Off asks every Warden on every trigger, makes no pre-filter call and starts no model server. `true` opts in. |
| `prefilter.baseUrl` | `http://127.0.0.1:8680` | The local System One server; loopback only. |
| `prefilter.model` | `kev-latest` | The server's model name. |
| `prefilter.skipBelow` | `0.26` | Skip a Warden when its score is below this. |
| `prefilter.timeoutMs` | `3000` | One call per trigger; past it every Warden is asked. |

**Measured** (`bun scripts/evals/warden-prefilter.ts measure`, 2026-10-14; the Prospector's 740 labelled moments, Opus run-1 labels, plus the 599 charter probes; this MacBook Pro M1 Max, 64 GB):

Recall is the share of (moment, Warden) pairs labelled relevant that are still asked; skip is the share of all pairs not asked. "r1" is the Opus run-1 labels on the 740 fixtures (the primary bar: broad, so conservative for a fail-open filter); "hand" is the 50 hand-checked fixtures; "probes" labels only each probe's gold Wardens (the rest count toward skips). Chance would skip 20% at 80% recall.

| Model (local, System One API) | Pairs | AUROC (r1) | Recall at 50% skip (r1) | Skip at 80% recall: r1 / hand / probes | Skip at 90% recall: r1 / hand / probes | Same decision on repeat | Latency per trigger p50 / p95 | Memory (physical) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Kev-4B (Qwen3.5-4B + LoRA, MLX bf16) | subset: 150 fixtures + 100 probes | 0.673 | 0.708 | 38% / 45% / 18% | 26% / 34% / 6% | 100% | 3.98 s / 4.62 s | 9.9 GB |
| Kev-0.8B (same subset) | 150 + 100 | 0.575 | 0.582 | 28% / 28% / 23% | 16% / 15% / 12% | 100% | 0.74 s / 0.88 s | 3.1 GB |
| Kev-0.8B (all) | 740 fixtures + 599 probes | 0.582 | 0.596 | 28% / 28% / 27% | 17% / 15% / 15% | 100% | 0.75 s / 0.88 s | 3.1 GB |
| Laya (ModernBERT-large) | 740 + 599 | 0.553 | 0.568 | 25% / 15% / 23% | 13% / 9% / 11% | 100% | 0.91 s / 1.25 s | 0.3 GB RSS |

By trigger, Kev-4B is best on the user's message (51% skipped at 80% recall, AUROC 0.74) and agent plans (45%), and weak on agent actions (25%) and finished turns (the probes, 18%). Within a Warden the topic Wardens separate (frontend, schema, security, types) and the process Wardens (intent, surface, verify, assumptions) do not.

**Status: not passing.** No model clears 80% recall with a skip rate worth its cost on this machine: Kev-0.8B is fast but barely beats chance, and Kev-4B adds 4–4.6 s before any Warden can start and about 10 GB. So the setting ships off by default.

Laya (ConvAI's ModernBERT-large decision model) was tried first and dropped: on the probes it recalled 0.53 of relevant Wardens while skipping half (chance is 0.5) and skipped only 23% at 80% recall; on the fixtures its AUROC was 0.55.
